questions.question: A cylinder of radius 4.5 cm and height 12 cm just fits in another cylinder completely with their axis perpendicular. What is the radius (in cm) of second cylinder?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For a cylinder (radius r, height h) fitting inside another cylinder with perpendicular axes:

The radius of the second cylinder R = √((h/2)² + r²)

Given r = 4.5 cm and h = 12 cm, then h/2 = 6 cm.

R = √(6² + 4.5²) = √(36 + 20.25) = √56.25 = 7.5 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 7.5 cm.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of the first cylinder (r₁) = 4.5 cm

Height of the first cylinder (h₁) = 12 cm

**Formula Used:**

When a cylinder is placed inside another with perpendicular axes, the radius of the outer cylinder (r₂) must be equal to the distance from the center of the inner cylinder to its farthest corner in the cross-section plane.

r₂ = √((h₁/2)² + r₁²)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8dae01dba955fd0672f7848dbfb7cf762bc7b00ab201719d51bee0e1c717f8bd.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the radius of the second cylinder be r₂.

⇒ r₂² = (h₁/2)² + r₁²

⇒ r₂² = (12/2)² + (4.5)²

⇒ r₂² = 6² + 20.25

⇒ r₂² = 36 + 20.25

⇒ r₂² = 56.25

⇒ r₂ = √56.25

⇒ r₂ = 7.5 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 7.5 cm.**

**__Additional Information__**

Cylinder Volume and Surface Area

The volume of a cylinder is V = πr²h, and the Total Surface Area is TSA = 2πr(r + h).

Pythagorean Theorem Application

In problems involving fitting shapes, the radius is often derived from the diagonal of the cross-section: Diagonal = √(Length² + Breadth²).

Perpendicular Axis Fitting

When a cylinder of (r₁, h₁) is placed inside another (r₂, h₂) with perpendicular axes, r₂ ≥ √((h₁/2)² + r₁²) and h₂ ≥ 2r₁.</p

questions.question: A right circular cylinder has height 28 cm and radius of base 14 cm. One hemisphere of radius 7 cm is cut from each of the two bases of the cylinder. What is the total surface area (in cm²) of the remaining part?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total Surface Area (TSA) = CSA of Cylinder + Area of 2 Bases (minus scoop openings) + CSA of 2 Hemispheres.

TSA = 2πRh + 2(πR² − πr²) + 2(2πr²) = 2π(Rh + R² + r²).

Given: R = 14 cm, h = 28 cm, r = 7 cm.

TSA = 2 × (22/7) × (14 × 28 + 14² + 7²) = (44/7) × (392 + 196 + 49).

TSA = 44 × 91 = 4004 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 4004 cm².**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of Cylinder (R) = 14 cm

Height of Cylinder (h) = 28 cm

Radius of Hemisphere (r) = 7 cm

**Formula Used:**

TSA of remaining part = 2πRh + 2πR² + 2πr²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/25a86e194892ff5c0f94dd1b34c2a2a731af188292b771f24904e85b0ca043e7.png] 

⇒ Area of curved surface of cylinder = 2 × (22/7) × 14 × 28

⇒ Area of curved surface = 44 × 56 = 2464 cm²

⇒ Remaining area of two bases = 2 × π × (R² − r²) = 2 × (22/7) × (14² − 7²)

⇒ Remaining area of bases = (44/7) × (196 − 49) = (44/7) × 147 = 44 × 21 = 924 cm²

⇒ Curved surface area of two internal hemispheres = 2 × (2 × π × r²) = 4 × (22/7) × 7 × 7

⇒ Internal CSA = 88 × 7 = 616 cm²

⇒ Total Surface Area = 2464 + 924 + 616

⇒ TSA = 4004 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 4004 cm².**

**__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area of Cylinder

The total surface area of a solid cylinder is given by 2πR(h + R), which includes the side curved area and two flat circular bases.

Surface Area of Hemisphere

The curved surface area is 2πr² and the total surface area (including the base) is 3πr².

Volume of Remaining Part

If required, the volume of this remaining part would be: Volume of Cylinder − 2 × Volume of Hemisphere = πR²h − (4/3)πr³.</p

questions.question: Two spheres of equal radius are taken out by cutting from a solid cube of side (12 + 4√3) cm. What is the maximum volume (in cm³) of each sphere?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For two equal spheres of radius r to be maximum inside a cube of side a, they are placed along the space diagonal.

Relation: 2r + 2r√3 = a√3 ⇒ 2r(1 + √3) = a√3

Given a = 12 + 4√3 = 4√3(√3 + 1)

2r(√3 + 1) = 4√3(√3 + 1) × √3 = 12(√3 + 1) ⇒ 2r = 12 ⇒ r = 6 cm

Volume = 4/3 × 22/7 × 6³ = 4/3 × 22/7 × 216 = 905.14 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 905.14 cm³.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Side of the solid cube (a) = (12 + 4√3) cm

Number of spheres = 2 (equal radius r)

**Formula Used:**

Space diagonal of cube = a√3

Distance from corner to center of sphere touching three faces = r√3

Volume of sphere = (4/3) × π × r³

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/67608b943109496aead420e097de08c1da8321ba676e9341fbd4a463a8af54ca.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total length along space diagonal = r√3 + 2r + r√3

⇒ a√3 = 2r√3 + 2r

⇒ a√3 = 2r(√3 + 1)

⇒ (12 + 4√3) × √3 = 2r(√3 + 1)

⇒ 12√3 + 4(3) = 2r(√3 + 1)

⇒ 12√3 + 12 = 2r(√3 + 1)

⇒ 12(√3 + 1) = 2r(√3 + 1)

⇒ 2r = 12

⇒ r = 6 cm

⇒ Volume of each sphere = (4/3) × (22/7) × 6 × 6 × 6

⇒ Volume = (4 × 22 × 2 × 36) ÷ 7

⇒ Volume = 6336 ÷ 7 ≈ 905.14 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 905.14 cm³.**

**__Additional Information__**

Sphere and Cube Properties

The longest rod that can fit in a cube is its space diagonal, given by a√3. For a single sphere of maximum volume inside a cube, the diameter equals the side (2r = a).

Surface Area of Sphere

The total surface area of a sphere is 4πr². In this problem, the surface area of each sphere would be 4 × 22/7 × 6² ≈ 452.57 cm².

Volume of Cube

The volume of the cube is side³. Here, V꜀ᵤbₑ = (12 + 4√3)³ cm³. The empty space is V꜀ᵤbₑ − 2 × Vₛₚₕₑᵣₑ.</p

questions.question: Three toys are in a shape of cylinder, hemisphere and cone. The three toys have same base. Height of each toy is 2√2 cm. What is the ratio of the total surface areas of cylinder, hemisphere and cone respectively?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**4 ∶ 3 ∶ [(√2) + 1]**__
**__Key Points__**
__

• Given that the three toys—a **cylinder**, a **hemisphere**, and a **cone**—have the same base and the same height.

• The **height (h)** of each toy is **2√2 cm**.

• For a **hemisphere**, the height is always equal to its **radius (r)**. Therefore, **r = h = 2√2 cm**.

• Since all three toys have the **same base**, they share the same radius **r = 2√2 cm**.

• **1. Total Surface Area (TSA) of the Cylinder:**
 The formula is **2πr(r + h)**.
 Substituting the values: TSA꜀yₗᵢₙdₑᵣ = 2 × π × 2√2 × (2√2 + 2√2)
 TSA꜀yₗᵢₙdₑᵣ = 4√2π × 4√2 = 16 × 2 × π = **32π**.

• **2. Total Surface Area (TSA) of the Hemisphere:**
 The formula is **3πr²**.
 Substituting the values: TSAₕₑₘᵢₛₚₕₑᵣₑ = 3 × π × (2√2)²
 TSAₕₑₘᵢₛₚₕₑᵣₑ = 3 × π × 8 = **24π**.

• **3. Total Surface Area (TSA) of the Cone:**
 The formula is **πr(r + l)**, where **l** is the **slant height**.
 First, find **l**: l = √(r² + h²) = √((2√2)² + (2√2)²) = √(8 + 8) = √16 = **4 cm**.
 Now, TSA꜀ₒₙₑ = π × 2√2 × (2√2 + 4)
 TSA꜀ₒₙₑ = π × (2√2 × 2√2 + 2√2 × 4) = π × (8 + 8√2) = **8π(1 + √2)**.

• **4. Calculating the Ratio:**
 Ratio = Cylinder TSA : Hemisphere TSA : Cone TSA
 Ratio = 32π : 24π : 8π(1 + √2)
 Dividing throughout by **8π**:
 Ratio = 4 : 3 : (1 + √2) or **4 ∶ 3 ∶ [(√2) + 1]**.

**Additional Information__**

• The **Curved Surface Area (CSA)** of these shapes are:
 
 
• Cylinder: **2πrh**
 
• Hemisphere: **2πr²**
 
• Cone: **πrl**
 

• The **Volume (V)** formulas for these shapes are:
 
 
• Cylinder: **πr²h**
 
• Hemisphere: **(2/3)πr³**
 
• Cone: **(1/3)πr²h**
 

• If the height and radius are equal (h = r), the ratio of their **volumes** (Cylinder : Hemisphere : Cone) is **3 : 2 : 1**.
